title: MBFT 814 Microbial Biotechnology: Complete Notes (full syllabus)

turns.input: Make detailed long-form notes for an M.Sc. Microbiology student covering every topic of MBFT 814 Microbial Biotechnology.
turns.output: 48-page notes, 18 chapters covering the whole syllabus: history and scope, bioreactors, fermentation types, screening and strain improvement, ethanol, glycerol, acetone-butanol-isopropanol, vinegar, lactic/citric/gluconic acids, riboflavin and B12, penicillin/streptomycin/tetracycline/griseofulvin, enzyme production, immobilization, SCP, biotransformation, all 5 practicals, plus a 29-fact revision sheet and question bank. 10 diagrams and flow charts.

turns.input: Make notes from the MSCMB syllabus, MBFT 814 Microbial Biotechnology (Semester III), only for the mid-term topics: introduction, history, types of bioreactors, types of fermentation, enzyme production, immobilization of enzymes, screening and strain improvement, antibiotic production, vitamin production. Use the class PDFs on history and bioreactors as reference.
turns.output: 10-page exam notes covering the 9 topics in order, with tables for bioreactor types, fermentation modes, SmF vs SSF, enzyme sources, immobilization methods, strain improvement, penicillin production, riboflavin and B12, plus exam-point boxes, an 18-fact quick-revision sheet and 10 likely questions.

turns.input: Make these MBFT 814 notes more detailed.
turns.output: Expanded from 10 to 29 pages: each topic now has full explanations, exam diagrams (batch growth curve, labelled stirred-tank fermenter, airlift, chemostat, 5 immobilization methods, enzyme and penicillin recovery flow charts), kinetics (Monod, chemostat), mutagen and screening tables, biosynthesis of penicillin, streptomycin/tetracycline/griseofulvin details, riboflavin and B12 processes, plus a 31-fact revision sheet and question bank.

turns.input: Make an assignment on Enterobacteriaceae from the lecture outline (G. Ebenezer Jeyakumar, 26 Sep): characters, source of isolation, identification steps, pathogenic and non-pathogenic members, infections, paracolon, classification, identification methods, motility, biochemical reactions, differentiating table, antigenic structure, phage types. Add a SHUATS front page with the university logo.
turns.output: Wrote a 16-section Word assignment covering all 13 outline points, with a SHUATS-style front page (logo, department, JIBB, P.I.D.), a contents page, an infections table, a lactose-grouping table and a 13-organism x 12-test differentiating table. Includes the 2016 Enterobacterales reclassification and 6 textbook/journal references.
